prerequisites: Second study section reached (at least 42 ECTS points from the first study section).
Experience with installing software packages on one's own computer.
Experience in operating an internet browser and setting security-relevant parameters (accepting cookies, licenses, saving passwords in the browser).

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the essential security risks and can assess their danger potential.
Students are able to independently perform a risk analysis and its evaluation.
Students are able to design an appropriate IT security strategy based on such a risk analysis, considering both organizational and technical aspects.
Students are able to assess the effectiveness of security strategies for practical application.
Students know the most important procedures for data encryption and authentication.
Students understand the essential mathematical concepts underlying the procedures for data encryption and authentication.

syllabus_topics: Organization and Security Management: Security models and security policies; Risk analysis of IT structure and IT-supported business processes

Network Security: Technical background to network risks; Security testing of networks (with tools, e.g., Nessus, manual tests); Malware and its defense; Procedures of hackers and crackers; Conception of firewalls and networks; Intrusion Detection and Monitoring
Making operating systems more secure; Secure configuration; "Hardening" an operating system (using capabilities, through tools, e.g., process isolation with AppArmor); Rootkits
Access Protection Systems: Authentication, various procedures; Rights systems on different levels
Software-related Vulnerabilities and their Prevention: Secure software development; Typical vulnerabilities such as buffer and heap overflows
Mathematical Background: Modular arithmetic; Finite groups; Finite fields
Public Key Procedures: RSA procedure; Diffie-Hellman key exchange; Signatures
assessment_rules: The examination is a written exam lasting 90 minutes. No further explanations are given.
bibliography: MATTHES, R. , 2003. Algebra, Kryptologie und Kodierungstheorie.
